How I work

Four commitments that hold whether the engagement is two weeks or two years.

One verify command per repository Lint, typecheck, test. CI runs exactly that command, so green on your machine means green on the branch.
Everything ships through a branch and a pipeline The deliberate step is the pipeline, not a person remembering to click something.
Self-hosted by default, on Hetzner and Caddy Postgres, systemd, hardware you can point at. No per-seat pricing, no vendor lock-in, no surprise invoice.
Handover is designed in from day one Standard stack, full data export, documentation written for the engineer who arrives after me.

Questions people actually ask

What happens if you are not available?

Fair, and it is why handover is in the contract from the start: a standard stack, one command that runs the whole check suite, CI any engineer can read, and complete data export. You are buying a system a normal team can pick up — not my availability. Ask your last agency for a full data export and time how long it takes.

How do I know AI-written code is any good?

You don't — and you wouldn't for hand-written code either. That is what tests and pipelines are for. Nothing reaches a hosted instance without the full suite passing, and I am accountable for the output regardless of what typed it.

We need someone on site, full time.

Then you need an employee, and I will tell you that rather than sell you four days a month that won't fix it. I am happy to help write the role and sit in on the technical interviews instead.

Can you do it cheaper?

Not by lowering the rate — by reducing the scope. Tell me which part can wait, and I'll re-quote the rest honestly.

Tell me what is in the way

Tell me what you are building and what is currently in the way. If I am not the right person, I will say so in the first reply rather than in the third meeting.
